title: Best Vitelliform Macular Dystrophy: A Clinical Compendium
summary: Best Disease is an autosomal dominant macular dystrophy characterized by the accumulation of lipofuscin-like material within and beneath the RPE. It classically manifests in childhood, progressing through distinct vitelliform stages from the 'egg-yolk' lesion to chorioretinal atrophy.

sections.title: Definition & Etiology
sections.content: Best Vitelliform Macular Dystrophy (BVMD) is an autosomal dominant retinal dystrophy caused by mutations in the BEST1 gene (11q13). This gene encodes bestrophin-1, a chloride channel located in the basolateral membrane of the Retinal Pigment Epithelium (RPE). Dysfunction leads to impaired fluid transport and toxic accumulation of lipofuscin, leading to photoreceptor degeneration.

rows: Dark choroid on FFA, fish-tail flecks

sections.title: The Diagnostic Gold Standard
content: Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF): Hyper-autofluorescence of the lesion due to lipofuscin accumulation.
OCT: Shows subretinal material collection, loss of IS/OS junction.
Genetic Testing: Targeted sequencing for BEST1 mutation confirmation.

content.explanation: B: Basolateral RPE channel dysfunction; E: EOG is abnormal; S: Scrambled egg appearance (stage 4); T: Toxic lipofuscin accumulation.

sections.title: Management Protocols
content: Step 1: Regular monitoring with OCT and Amsler grid for CNV detection.
Step 2: Low vision rehabilitation if visual acuity drops.
Step 3: Anti-VEGF therapy (Intravitreal Ranibizumab/Aflibercept) if CNV develops.
Step 4: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) if CNV is extrafoveal (historical, now rarely used).
